segments.en: You can also get some blood exams done.

segments.en: Go to the Red Cross and donate blood.

segments.zh: 一个人说他和一些护理人员一起去了。

segments.zh: 所以护理人员是一个人。

segments.en: It's a person.
segments.zh: 这是一个人。

segments.en: It's a profession, right?
segments.zh: 这是职业，对吧？

segments.en: To be a paramedic.
segments.zh: 成为一名护理人员。

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.en: But it's not really a doctor.
segments.zh: 但这不是真正的医生。

segments.en: So paramedics are something like nurses, right?
segments.zh: 所以护理人员就像护士一样，对吧？

segments.en: That travel in an ambulance and get to an emergency or get to the scene of an accident and help out a person.
segments.zh: 乘坐救护车前往紧急情况或到达事故现场并帮助一个人。

segments.en: So they immobilize the person, they give them oxygen.
segments.zh: 所以他们固定了人，给他们氧气。

segments.en: They make sure that they stay alive until they reach the hospital.
segments.zh: 他们确保他们活着，直到他们到达医院。

segments.en: Okay, so a paramedic, you might hear the word medic, it's the same thing.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个护理人员，你可能会听到医生这个词，这是一样的。

segments.en: A paramedic is like a nurse.
segments.zh: 护理人员就像护士。

segments.en: They're not a doctor, but they're usually the first person to help when there's been an accident or a disaster.
segments.zh: 他们不是医生，但他们通常是发生事故或灾难时第一个提供帮助的人。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So if there is an earthquake and many people are stuck in the buildings, usually paramedics will be the ones on the scene trying to get them out and helping them by applying for first aid.
segments.zh: 因此，如果发生地震并且许多人被困在建筑物中，通常情况下，医护人员将成为现场的人，试图通过申请急救来帮助他们。

segments.en: Well, after that, we have finally some of the injuries that a paramedic might see.
segments.zh: 好吧，在那之后，我们终于有了护理人员可能看到的一些伤害。

segments.en: The first injury is usually associated with the head.
segments.zh: 第一次损伤通常与头部有关。

segments.en: This is called a concussion.
segments.zh: 这称为脑震荡。

segments.en: You suffered a concussion.
segments.zh: 你遭受了脑震荡。

segments.en: It sounds painful.
segments.zh: 听起来很痛苦。

segments.en: Yeah, it does.
segments.zh: 是的，确实如此。

segments.en: And actually, it's very common, I think, right?
segments.zh: 实际上，我认为这很常见，对吧？

segments.en: If you fall and you hit your head.
segments.zh: 如果你摔倒了，你撞到了你的头。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a concussion is really when your brain hits your skull.
segments.zh: 所以当你的大脑撞到你的头骨时，脑震荡真的是。

segments.en: That's the bone that protects your brain.
segments.zh: 那是保护你的大脑的骨头。

segments.en: So really, you're hitting your head really, really hard.
segments.zh: 所以真的，你真的非常非常努力地击中了你的头。

segments.en: And usually, this can have some bad side effects like you lose your memory or you're a little bit confused.
segments.zh: 通常，这可能会产生一些不良副作用，例如您会失去记忆，或者您有点困惑。

segments.en: It's very common with football players.
segments.zh: 这在足球运动员中很常见。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: With any contact sport, if people suffer concussions, and it's just like, imagine when you have a DVD player and you hit it and the disc skips or it goes back.
segments.zh: 对于任何接触性运动，如果人们遭受脑震荡，就像，想象一下，当您有一台 DVD 播放器并击中它并且光盘跳过或它会退回时，请想象一下。

segments.en: That's kind of what happens to your brain.
segments.zh: 这就是你的大脑发生的事情。

segments.en: So you can suffer memory loss.
segments.zh: 所以你可能会遭受记忆丧失。

segments.en: You can even lose your sight temporarily.
segments.zh: 你甚至可以暂时失明。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this can be very serious and obviously should be looked at by a paramedic.
segments.zh: 所以这可能非常严重，显然应该由护理人员查看。

segments.en: We also have another situation that is similarly serious.
segments.zh: 我们还有另一个同样严重的情况。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what is a fracture or two fracture?
segments.zh: 那么什么是骨折或两次骨折？

segments.en: A fracture is a thing.

segments.en: It's a break.

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you could say, I broke my arm.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，我摔断了手臂。

segments.en: But you could also say, I fractured my arm.
segments.zh: 但你也可以说，我的手臂骨折了。

segments.en: This is the more medical term.
segments.zh: 这是更医学的术语。

segments.en: But of course, there are different ways to break something.
segments.zh: 但当然，有不同的方法可以打破某些东西。

segments.en: And so in medicine, we have a compound fracture.
segments.zh: 所以在医学上，我们有复合骨折。

segments.en: So a compound fracture is pretty painful and it's a little bit more serious.
segments.zh: 所以复合骨折是相当痛苦的，而且更严重一些。

segments.en: You have a simple fracture, which is when your bone just breaks.
segments.zh: 你有一个简单的骨折，这就是你的骨头刚刚断裂。

segments.en: Or a hairline, which means that there's a little thin part where it's broken, but it's not really serious.
segments.zh: 或发际线，这意味着它有一个很薄的部分被打破，但它并不严重。

segments.en: In this case, it's your bones actually push towards each other.

segments.en: Or they're on top of each other.

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.en: It's like that, but it's your bone.

segments.en: So it's extremely painful.

segments.en: Yeah, yeah.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: It's very, very painful.
segments.zh: 这是非常非常痛苦的。

segments.en: Wow.

segments.en: Yeah.

segments.zh: 所以，是的，如果你晕倒了，基本上就是你只是站在那里，你坐在某个地方，突然间，一切都变黑了，你醒来，你就在地上。

segments.en: What is the first thing that a paramedic does when he or she finds a body in an emergency?
segments.zh: 当护理人员在紧急情况下找到尸体时，他或她会做的第一件事是什么？

segments.en: What paramedic checks for a pulse to make sure you're alive, right?
segments.zh: 什么护理人员会检查脉搏以确保您还活着，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: A pulse.
segments.zh: 一个脉冲。

segments.en: So, dum, dum, dum, dum.
segments.zh: 所以，dum，dum，dum，dum。

segments.en: The pulse is the rhythm, that's the sound of your heart pumping blood.
segments.zh: 脉搏是节奏，那是你的心脏跳动的声音。

segments.en: And you can feel someone's wrist or their throat.
segments.zh: 你可以感觉到某人的手腕或喉咙。

segments.en: So to check for a pulse means to check and make sure their heart is pumping blood.
segments.zh: 因此，检查脉搏意味着检查并确保他们的心脏在抽血。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And not only that, but to make sure that the heart is pumping blood relatively normal because sometimes your heart can be pumping blood too fast or too slow.

segments.en: And if it's too slow, it's very possible that you will faint.
segments.zh: 如果它太慢，你很可能会晕倒。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we check for a pulse.

segments.en: Now, what else happens?
segments.zh: 现在，还会发生什么？

segments.en: Well, if there's a very serious emergency and the paramedic needs help to give aid to the person who is injured, then they will rush that person to the hospital.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果有一个非常严重的紧急情况，并且护理人员需要帮助来帮助受伤的人，那么他们就会将那个人送往医院。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the verb to rush, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 所以动词要匆忙，这是什么意思？

segments.en: All right, so to rush someone or to rush someone to the hospital means to take someone or to go with someone very, very quickly.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以赶某人或把某人赶到医院意味着非常非常快地带某人或与某人一起去。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's give an example.
segments.zh: 所以让我们举个例子。

segments.en: I could say, listen, Marco, I don't want to rush you, but I really need the report done today.
segments.zh: 我可以说，听着，马可，我不想催你，但我真的需要今天完成的报告。

segments.en: Or I could say, I need to rush home.
segments.zh: 或者我可以说，我需要赶回家。

segments.en: My parents need me.
segments.zh: 我的父母需要我。

segments.en: Or if a woman is having a baby, you want to rush her to the emergency room.
segments.zh: 或者，如果一个女人正在生孩子，你想把她送到急诊室。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you need to go quickly.
segments.zh: 所以你需要快点走。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So when we're talking about fainting, the person said, before he used the word faint, he said, I tend to faint.
segments.zh: 所以当我们谈论晕倒时，那个人说，在他使用昏迷这个词之前，他说，我倾向于晕倒。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I tend to.
segments.zh: 我倾向于。

segments.en: I tend to is a really great verb that describes a normal or habitual behavior.
segments.zh: 我倾向于是一个非常好的动词，它描述了正常或习惯性的行为。

segments.en: That's like saying, I tend to faint when it's very, very hot outside.
segments.zh: 这就像说，当外面非常非常热时，我往往会晕倒。

segments.en: That means I often faint when it's very, very hot outside.
segments.zh: 这意味着当外面非常非常热时，我经常会晕倒。

segments.en: It's something that happens normally.
segments.zh: 这是正常发生的事情。

segments.en: So it's a tendency.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种倾向。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's not for everyone.
segments.zh: 它不适合所有人。

segments.en: It's for me.
segments.zh: 是给我的。

segments.en: So I tend to.
segments.zh: 所以我倾向于。

segments.en: What's something that you tend to faint when you see?
segments.zh: 当你看到时，你会晕倒的东西是什么？

segments.en: I never faint.
segments.zh: 我从不晕倒。

segments.en: You don't faint.
segments.zh: 你不晕倒。

segments.en: No, just kidding.
segments.zh: 不，只是开玩笑。

segments.en: But you know what?
segments.zh: 不过你知道吗？

segments.en: I tend to leave the towel on the bed sometimes after I take a shower.
segments.zh: 有时我洗完澡后会把毛巾放在床上。

segments.en: I know it's a bad habit.
segments.zh: 我知道这是一个坏习惯。

segments.en: And then the sheets smell.
segments.zh: 然后床单闻起来。

segments.en: No, they don't.
segments.zh: 不，并不是。

segments.en: Because I leave it there for like five or 10 minutes and then I realize, oh my God, and then I pick it up.
segments.zh: 因为我把它留在那里五到十分钟，然后我意识到，天哪，然后我把它捡起来。

segments.en: But it's hard to...
segments.zh: 但是很难...

segments.en: That's gross.
segments.zh: 真恶心。

segments.en: No, it's not.
segments.zh: 不，不是。

segments.en: I tend to forget my leftover food in the refrigerator for a long time.
segments.zh: 我往往会在冰箱里忘记剩下的食物很长时间。

segments.en: And then it starts to smell.
segments.zh: 然后它开始闻起来。

segments.en: That's gross.
segments.zh: 真恶心。

segments.en: But I don't like to waste food.
segments.zh: 但我不喜欢浪费食物。

segments.en: But you like let it rot and then your fridge smells.
segments.zh: 但是你喜欢让它腐烂，然后你的冰箱闻起来。

segments.en: It happens.
segments.zh: 它发生了。

segments.en: So that's all we've got for Fluency Builder today.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天为 Flueny Builder 所拥有的一切。

segments.en: But we can talk about tendencies in a moment.
segments.zh: 但我们可以在一瞬间谈论倾向。

segments.en: Maybe a homework assignment could be to think of something that you tend to do.
segments.zh: 也许家庭作业可能是想想你倾向于做的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That could be an interesting homework assignment.
segments.zh: 这可能是一个有趣的家庭作业。

segments.en: But before we jump into that, why don't we listen to our dialogue for the very last time?
segments.zh: 但在我们开始之前，我们为什么不听我们的对话最后一次呢？

segments.en: Hey, Joe, where have you been these past few days?
segments.zh: 嘿，乔，这几天你去哪儿了？

segments.en: I've been busy with a first aid course that I started about a week ago at the Red Cross.
segments.zh: 我一直忙于大约一周前在红十字会开始的急救课程。

segments.en: Cool.
segments.zh: 真不错。

segments.en: I've always wanted to do something like that.
segments.zh: 我一直想做这样的事情。

segments.en: Have you learned anything useful?
segments.zh: 你学到了什么有用的东西吗？

segments.en: For sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: I mean, we learned how to apply pressure to stop bleeding, how to check for a pulse, and even how to apply CPR.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，我们学会了如何施加压力来止血，如何检查脉搏，甚至如何应用心肺复苏术。

segments.en: Have you treated any real emergencies?
segments.zh: 您是否处理过任何真正的紧急情况？

segments.en: Well, they took us along with some paramedics.
segments.zh: 他们带我们跟着急救人员一起出勤。

segments.en: There was this guy who fell off his motorcycle and suffered a concussion as well as a couple of compound fractures.
segments.zh: 有个人从摩托车上摔了下来，造成脑震荡，还有几处开放性骨折。

segments.en: His wounds were pretty serious, so they had to rush him to the hospital.
segments.zh: 他的伤口很严重，所以他们不得不把他送到医院。

segments.en: It was intense.
segments.zh: 那真激烈。

segments.en: I can imagine.
segments.zh: 我能想象。

segments.en: I tend to faint when I see blood, so I think I won't be taking up a course like that anytime soon.
segments.zh: 当我看到血液时，我往往会晕倒，所以我想我不会很快参加这样的课程。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So that's all the time we have for today.
segments.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里。

segments.en: Be sure to do your homework assignment.
segments.zh: 一定要做你的家庭作业。

segments.en: Come to EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 来 EnglishPod.com 吧。

segments.en: In the comments section, tell us, what do you tend to do?
segments.zh: 在评论部分，告诉我们，您倾向于做什么？

segments.en: It could be a good thing.
segments.zh: 这可能是一件好事。

segments.en: It could be a bad thing.
segments.zh: 这可能是一件坏事。

segments.en: Obviously, you can try and use some of the vocabulary you heard in today's lesson about health and safety.
segments.zh: 显然，您可以尝试使用您在今天的健康和安全课程中听到的一些词汇。

segments.en: You might get some extra points from us for doing that.
segments.zh: 您可能会从我们那里获得一些额外的积分。

segments.en: I know some people who tend to leave the house with a whole medicine kit in their bags or in their purses.
segments.zh: 我知道有些人倾向于在袋子或钱包里带着整个药包离开家。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: A first aid kit.
segments.zh: 急救箱。

segments.en: A first aid kit, exactly.
segments.zh: 一个急救箱，确切地说。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: So do you do this?
segments.zh: 那你这样做吗？

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: That's all we've got for today, so until next time.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天所拥有的一切，所以直到下一次。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
